question: Which cells, also called neurilemma cells, are the main glial cells in the PNS and play an essential role in the survival and functions of neurons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Schwann cells.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Schwann cells** are the main glial cells in the **PNS.**
 
• They provide **myelin sheath** around the axons of neurons, which helps in faster **conduction of nerve impulses.**
 
• Schwann cells also play a crucial role in the **regeneration of damaged axons.**
 
• They are also involved in the maintenance of the **ionic environment **around the neurons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bipolar cells** are specialized neurons found in the **retina of the eye, **which help in** transmitting signals **from** photoreceptor cells** to ganglion cells
 
• **Ganglion cells** are the output neurons of the **retina**, which **transmit visual information** to the brain via the optic nerve.
 
• **Photoreceptor cells** are specialized cells found in the **retina of the eye, **which help in detecting light and converting it into **neural signals.**
